title: The Clock That Detonates Into Gold
source: Benjamin Franklin, Advice to a Young Tradesman, 1748 (public domain)
caption:
Remember that time is money. Benjamin Franklin wrote it in 1748. Start early: time is the one thing compound interest cannot buy back. Educational content, not financial advice.

prompt: Hyper-realistic, photorealistic 10-second vertical 9:16 sequence in one continuous impossible shot, no cuts, violent kinetic camera. ONE character only, no other people. Character: a lean man in his seventies, narrow face, trimmed white beard, round wire-rim glasses, bald on top with wild white hair at the sides whipping in the wind, long dark indigo wool coat flapping sideways, fierce amused grey eyes. Realm: a colossal brass clock tower the size of a mountain floats in a violet thunderstorm sky, its giant clock face is one enormous embossed gold coin with no numerals, the minute hand is a ten meter iron beam. Struggle: the man hangs one-handed from the tip of the minute hand, boots kicking over a bottomless drop, coat tearing in the gale, lightning flashing behind him, sparks spraying from the gears. Timing: 0 to 2 seconds, a fast whip-pan from the storm into a low-angle orbit around him as the hand jolts forward tick by tick. At 2.5 seconds a snap-zoom onto his face, he locks eyes with the lens and shouts in a gravelly commanding old man voice, American accent, slow and clear: Remember that time is money. His lips move exactly with these five words and nothing else is spoken. At the word time the clock hand freezes mid-swing and every cloud stops dead for one beat. At the word money the giant gold coin face detonates outward in a blast of molten gold, a million coins explode toward the lens like a meteor storm and a shockwave ripples through the clouds. From 6 to 10 seconds a rapid crane-up and pull-back reveals the whole tower raining gold into the abyss while he swings up onto the hand and stands laughing, coat blazing in golden light. Style: epic IMAX fantasy, chiaroscuro lightning, volumetric god-rays, molten gold glow, anamorphic flares, fine 35mm grain, 24fps. Audio: his voice, thunder, grinding gears and the roar of coins, no music. Strict rules: one person only, same face and coat in every frame, mouth clearly articulating, no subtitles, no text or numbers anywhere, no logos, no morphing.

title: Three Baskets Over The Lava

caption:
